Notes: 1st M1 for attempting to divide (one term correct). 1st A1 for both terms correct on the same line, accept $3x^1$ for $3x$ or $\frac{2}{x}$ for $2x^{-1}$. questions.stem: A farmer has a pay scheme to keep fruit pickers working throughout the 30 day season. He pays £$a$ for their first day, £$(a+d)$ for their second day, £$(a+2d)$ for their third day, and so on, thus increasing the daily payment by £$d$ for each extra day they work.

parts.label: a
parts.text:
A picker who works for all 30 days will earn £40.75 on the final day.

(a) Use this information to form an equation in $a$ and $d$.
(2)
parts.mark_scheme:
M1: $a+29d=40.75$ or $a=40.75-29d$ or $29d=40.75-a$ for attempt to use $a+(n-1)d$ with $n=30$ to form an equation. So $a+(30-1)d=$ any number is OK
A1: as written. Must see $29d$ not just $(30-1)d$. Ignore any floating £ signs e.g. $a+29d=£40.75$ is OK for M1A1. These two marks must be scored in (a). Some may omit (a) but get correct equation in (c) [or (b)] but we do not give the marks retrospectively.

parts.label: b
parts.text:
A picker who works for all 30 days will earn a total of £1005

(b) Show that $15(a+40.75)=1005$
(2)
parts.mark_scheme:
M1: $(S_{30}=)\frac{30}{2}(a+l)$ or $\frac{30}{2}(a+40.75)$ or $\frac{30}{2}(2a+(30-1)d)$ or $15(2a+29d)$ for an attempt to use an $S_n$ formula with $n=30$. Must see one of the printed forms ($S_{30}=$ is not required)
A1 cso: So $1005=15[a+40.75]$ * for forming an equation with 1005 and $S_n$ and simplifying to printed answer. Condone £ signs e.g. $15[a+£40.75]=1005$ is OK for A1. Parts (b) and (c) may run together.

parts.label: c
parts.text:
(c) Hence find the value of $a$ and the value of $d$.
(4)
parts.mark_scheme:
M1: $67=a+40.75$ for an attempt to simplify the given linear equation for $a$. Correct processes. Must get to $ka=\ldots$ or $k=a+m$ i.e. one step (division or subtraction) from $a=\ldots$. Commonly $15a=1005-611.25(=393.75)$
A1: so $a=(£)26.25$ or $2625$p or $26\frac{1}{4}$ NOT $\frac{105}{4}$ or any other fraction
M1: $29d=40.75-26.25$ for correct attempt at a linear equation for $d$, follow through their $a$ or equation in (a). Equation just has to be linear in $d$, they don't have to simplify to $d=\ldots$
A1: $=14.5$ so $d=(£)0.50$ or $50$p or $\frac{1}{2}$. Depends upon 2nd M1 and use of correct $a$. Do not penalise a second time if there were minor arithmetic errors in finding $a$ provided $a=26.25$ (o.e.) is used. Do not accept other fractions other than $\frac{1}{2}$. If answer is in pence a "p" must be seen.
Sim Equ alternative: Use this scheme: 1st M1A1 for $a$ and 2nd M1A1 for $d$. Typically solving: $1005=30a+435d$ and $40.75=a+29d$. If they find $d$ first then follow through use of their $d$ when finding $a$.

questions.stem:
The curve $C$ has equation $y=\mathrm{f}(x)$, $x>0$, where
$\frac{dy}{dx}=3x-\frac{5}{\sqrt{x}}-2$

Given that the point $P(4, 5)$ lies on $C$, find

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) $\mathrm{f}(x)$,
(5)
parts.mark_scheme:
M1 A1 A1: $(y=)\frac{3x^2}{2}-\frac{5x^{\frac{1}{2}}}{\frac{1}{2}}-2x\ (+c)$
M1: $\mathrm{f}(4)=5 \Rightarrow 5=\frac{3}{2}\times 16-10\times 2-8+c$
A1: $c=9$
$\left[\mathrm{f}(x)=\frac{3}{2}x^2-10x^{\frac{1}{2}}-2x+9\right]$
Notes: 1st M1 for an attempt to integrate $x^n\to x^{n+1}$. 1st A1 for at least 2 correct terms in $x$ (unsimplified). 2nd A1 for all 3 terms in $x$ correct (condone missing $+c$ at this point). Needn't be simplified. 2nd M1 for using the point $(4,5)$ to form a linear equation for $c$. Must use $x=4$ and $y=5$ and have no $x$ term and the function must have "changed". 3rd A1 for $c=9$. The final expression is not required.

parts.label: b
parts.text:
(b) an equation of the tangent to $C$ at the point $P$, giving your answer in the form $ax+by+c=0$, where $a$, $b$ and $c$ are integers.
(4)
parts.mark_scheme:
M1: $m=3\times 4-\frac{5}{2}-2\left(=7.5\ \text{or}\ \frac{15}{2}\right)$ for an attempt to evaluate $\mathrm{f}'(4)$. Some correct use of $x=4$ in $\mathrm{f}'(x)$ but condone slips. They must therefore have at least $3\times 4$ or $-\frac{5}{2}$ and clearly be using $\mathrm{f}'(x)$ with $x=4$. Award this mark wherever it is seen.
M1 A1: Equation is: $y-5=\frac{15}{2}(x-4)$ for using their value of $m$ [or their $-\frac{1}{m}$] (provided it clearly comes from using $x=4$ in $\mathrm{f}'(x)$) to form an equation of the line through $(4,5)$. Allow this mark for an attempt at a normal or tangent. Their $m$ must be numerical. Use of $y=mx+c$ scores this mark when $c$ is found. 1st A1 for any correct expression for the equation of the line
A1: $2y-15x+50=0$ o.e. for any correct equation with integer coefficients. An "=" is required, e.g. $2y=15x-50$ etc as long as the equation is correct and has integer coefficients.
Normal: Attempt at normal can score both M marks in (b) but A0A0
